joint_recovery.position_reference_note: Same rule as P0 (the controller's own position target), extended to RAPTOR: its internal target is not published on trajectory_setpoint, so while RAPTOR owns the actuators the target is its logged capture (activation reset or setpoint-stale hold); classic stages use trajectory_setpoint as in P0. trajectory_setpoint-only and fixed NED results are kept as comparisons.

short_stage_rule.rule: A recovery stage (P0 definition: between actual owner changes, truncated at the next request) shorter than joint_recovery.dwell_s cannot reach SETTLED by definition. Such a stage is reported as INSUFFICIENT_OBSERVATION and marked planned_short_stage instead of failing the run verdict. All thresholds are unchanged. In P3 only the D1 classic deactivation (0.3 s) is pre-registered as short; p3_metrics requires every other stage of the run to be SETTLED and the exempt stage to be exactly that one.

p2.purpose: P5 E1/E4 (P2 kinds). E1: C->N while the classic cruises at 1.0/2.0/3.0 m/s (P4-01c V-profiles, mechanism and measurement unchanged), along +N (A0), along north-east (A45, heading unchanged) or along +N with the vehicle spawned at yaw +45 deg (Y45: same flight direction relative to the heading as A45, world rotated). N2 memory (RINI=4) everywhere; T0 zero-velocity activation capture, T1 speed-matched activation target (RTGT=1, 2.0 m/s^2). E4: RAPTOR tracks the external 2.0 m/s line, the stream stops and the classic AUTO_LOITER takes over (p2_n_to_c).

V1.0-A0.description: E1 1.0 m/s: P4-01c V1.0 profile (hold 3 s, 2 s ramp, 4.0 s cruise, C->N at the end of the cruise), along +N (heading 96 deg; flight direction -96 deg from the heading, 6 deg from the lateral target axis). Same path length and planned-path check as 01c (Euclidean radius does not depend on the direction). Flight failures are results.

V1.0-A45.description: E1 1.0 m/s: P4-01c V1.0 profile (hold 3 s, 2 s ramp, 4.0 s cruise, C->N at the end of the cruise), along north-east (heading 96 deg unchanged; flight direction -51 deg from the heading, 6 deg from the target-frame diagonal). Same path length and planned-path check as 01c (Euclidean radius does not depend on the direction). Flight failures are results.

Same path length and planned-path check as 01c (Euclidean radius does not depend on the direction). Flight failures are results.

Same path length and planned-path check as 01c (Euclidean radius does not depend on the direction). Flight failures are results.

N2.0.description: E4: RAPTOR (external setpoints) on the P4-01c V2.0 profile along +N (hold 3 s, 2 s ramp to 2.0 m/s, 1.75 s cruise); at the end of the cruise the stream stops and the classic takes over in AUTO_LOITER (p2_n_to_c). Budget as V2.0 (the 1.0 m v^2/(2a) term covers the AUTO_LOITER braking). Flight failures are results.

T0.description: N2 memory; original RAPTOR takeover target: activation capture of the current position and yaw with zero velocity (MC_RAPTOR_RTGT=0, the default)

T1.description: N2 memory; speed-matched takeover target: activation capture of the current position and yaw with the current horizontal velocity (vertical 0), then a fixed 2.0 m/s^2 deceleration along that direction to zero, target position integrated from the target velocity, then hold at the end point (MC_RAPTOR_RTGT=1, MC_RAPTOR_RTDEC=2.0)

C0.description: E4 N->C: N2 memory (RINI=4) at RAPTOR's setup entry in hover; the classic takes over in its original AUTO_LOITER without classic-side treatment (NCO=0)

p2.reference: Before the subject event the outgoing controller tracks one runner-published trajectory_setpoint (position ramp, velocity and acceleration feed-forward, constant yaw) starting from its own current target: classic through OFFBOARD, RAPTOR through its external trajectory_setpoint input. At the event the stream stops and the incoming controller uses its original mechanism: RAPTOR captures its takeover target in the activation cycle (T0: activation position/yaw with zero velocity; T1: same capture with the current horizontal velocity, then a fixed deceleration); classic AUTO_LOITER brakes to the navigator loiter point.
p2.baselines: p1_baseline_classic: classic OFFBOARD motion then AUTO_LOITER (same takeover mechanism, no controller switch). p1_baseline_raptor: RAPTOR external-setpoint motion then the stream stops; after RAPTOR's 200 ms setpoint timeout it holds its position (same capture rule as mode entry, no reset or switch).

motor_saturation.note: actuator_motors control in [0,1]; upper/lower limit within 1e-3

p2.motor_rms_definition: RMS over [change, change+0.5 s] and the four motors of (run actuator_motors - in-batch baseline mean curve), zero-order hold on a 1 ms grid aligned at each run's actual change; baseline = same-controller baseline of the same condition in the same batch.
p2.elimination_ratio_definition: (N0 - Nx) / (N0 - baseline) per metric, from in-batch group means (motor step at change, max altitude loss, motor RMS deviation).

failure_criteria.safety_envelope: any of tilt >= 45 deg, angular-rate component >= 8 rad/s, horizontal radius >= 10 m, altitude >= 8 m (frozen safety envelope; reaching the limit counts), or a runner safety abort
failure_criteria.no_joint_recovery: joint recovery not SETTLED within 10 s after the actual change (frozen P0 thresholds, active controller target)
failure_criteria.motor_saturation: any motor at >=0.999 or <=0.001 continuously for at least 0.5 s inside [trigger, window end]

exploration.note: only failure_criteria are used (P2 flight_outcome); P4 has no exploration levels

host.clocks: jetson_clocks applied 2026-10-15 (all 14 CPUs 2601 MHz, CPU idle states off, EMC 4266 MHz, nvpmodel 120W); verified before each batch from /sys and recorded in the batch host.json
host.note: taskset pinning of the processes the runner starts; other host processes are not isolated (no isolcpus). Remote desktop disconnected during batches.

planned_path_check.rule: Before the reference motion starts the runner checks that origin + planned path to the event point (ramp + cruise) + the speed-matched target's stop distance v^2/(2a) (a = 2.0 m/s^2) + the 1.0 m margin stays inside safety_radius_m - radius_margin_m = 8 m; otherwise the run fails before moving. A level that cannot fit is not flown. Cruise lengths are chosen so that every level fits (conditions.*.safety_budget_m).

p3.purpose: P4-01a (D2 hover re-entry, statistical confirmation) and P4-01b M3 (second C->N during classic 1 m/s cruise): P3 sequence and measurement.

sequence.mechanism: Every C->N starts from classic OFFBOARD tracking one runner-published stationary trajectory_setpoint at the current target; the stream stops and RAPTOR's mode is requested at once (P2 S1 mechanism), so RAPTOR captures its target in the activation cycle (activation_reset_hold, zero velocity). After the first C->N the runner restarts the stationary stream at RAPTOR's exact captured position and yaw (RAPTOR external setpoint input, no target change). N->C requests OFFBOARD with that stream running: the classic takeover target is RAPTOR's own target (NCO=0, no state intervention). Rationale: AUTO_LOITER republishes valid trajectory_setpoints that RAPTOR then follows for its 200 ms timeout before capturing (seen in P2 setup entries), and a 0.3 s deactivation cannot pass through AUTO_LOITER and back into OFFBOARD. The final N->C before landing is AUTO_LOITER as in P1/P2 (not measured).

D2.description: 10 s classic deactivation at the hover point

R.description: RAPTOR continuous hover baseline: after the first C->N RAPTOR keeps tracking the stationary stream for the D2-equivalent 10 s, then the stream stops and RAPTOR re-captures after its 200 ms setpoint timeout (virtual second takeover, P2 S1 baseline mechanism)

M3.description: P3 sequence; after the N->C at the hover point the classic holds 3 s (the N->C stage settles before any motion), then follows the P2 S3 profile along +N (2 s linear ramp to 1.0 m/s, 4 s cruise); the second C->N is requested 9 s after the N->C request, during the cruise. Same state at the event as an M1 C->N; the old exit memory (N3) was formed in hover.

safety_check.rule: Before the deactivation motion the runner checks that the planned point at the second C->N (ramp_cruise: the cruise position at deactivation_s; D3: the trapezoid end) plus the braking allowance (if given) lies inside safety_radius_m - radius_margin_m from the origin; otherwise the run fails before moving.

N0.description: original reset at the second entry

N3.description: old memory: GRU and previous action stored by RAPTOR on the first inactive cycle after the first exit, held unchanged during the deactivation, written back at re-entry

N2s.description: memory formed by the shadow inference during the deactivation (own unexecuted actions as previous action), kept at re-entry

N2.description: teacher forcing during the deactivation (classic applied motors as previous action); at re-entry GRU kept and previous action = classic last applied command

p3.treatment_rule: MC_RAPTOR_RINI=0 and MC_RAPTOR_NCO=0 are set before arming (first C->N is N0 for every run). The treatment value is set (param set, read back) 1 s after the first entry while RAPTOR is active, so it is in force for the whole deactivation and the second entry. Teacher forcing only acts while RAPTOR is inactive; mode-entry writes only at entry.

motor_saturation.note: actuator_motors control in [0,1]; upper/lower limit within 1e-3

p3.motor_rms_definition: RMS over [change, change+0.5 s] and the four motors of (run actuator_motors - in-batch RAPTOR continuous-hover baseline mean curve aligned at its re-capture), 1 ms zero-order hold. N->C: RMS against the run's own classic mean command in the 0.5 s before the first C->N request, over [change, min(change+0.5 s, next request)).
p3.elimination_ratio_definition: (N0 - Nx) / (N0 - baseline) per metric and deactivation condition, from in-batch group means (second C->N).

entry_check.teacher_forcing_window: inactive inference rows strictly after the N->C owner change and before the second C->N owner change (the shadow inference in the owner-change tick runs before the classic first command and is reported separately)

memory_length.method: Exact offline replay of the frozen policy (Dense 22-16 ReLU, GRU 16, Dense 16-4) on logged SITL inputs: raptor_input observation and research_memory previous_action averaged over the control calls since the last native step (rl_tools executor action_history), native steps only. Validated per run by reproducing the logged GRU from the logged state. Memory length = native steps (and seconds) after which the GRU replayed from a different initial memory stays within the threshold of the GRU with the complete history, on the same logged inputs.
memory_length.sitl_teacher_forcing: N2 runs: teacher forcing starts at the N->C; distance of the logged teacher-forced GRU to the replay with the complete teacher-forced history is undefined in closed loop, so the measured quantity is the replay of the logged deactivation inputs from zero and from the exit memory against the logged GRU, plus the direct research_memory distance to the late-deactivation mean (D2).

criteria.safety_envelope: any of tilt >= 45 deg, angular-rate component >= 8 rad/s, horizontal radius >= 10 m, altitude >= 8 m (frozen safety envelope; reaching the limit counts), or a runner safety abort
criteria.no_joint_recovery: joint recovery not SETTLED within 10 s after the actual change (frozen P0 thresholds, active controller target)
criteria.motor_saturation: any motor at >=0.999 or <=0.001 continuously for at least 0.5 s inside [trigger, window end]

flight_failures.rule: Pre-registered flight failures (frozen criteria above, all infrastructure checks passing) are results and do not stop the batch, as approved for the P2 N->C batches; any infrastructure or evidence failure stops the batch.

equivalence.purpose: New candidate (adds MC_RAPTOR_RINI=6 and the exit-memory store) must reproduce P2 S1 with the P2 kinds and config before P3.
equivalence.metric_rule: each run inside [min - t, max + t] of the P2 group with the same treatment (N0: s1a+s1b, N2: s1a), t = max(tolerance, half the reference spread)
required: P2 entry and teacher-forcing evidence VERIFIED, capture activation_reset_hold with zero target velocity
written GRU norm (N2) inside the P2 range with the same rule (tolerance 0.05)

dev_latency.rule: 10 P3 sequences on the final binary before freezing; every run's maximum applied-command age must stay <= 8 ms (P2 dev-04 level) with the frozen gate unchanged (p99 4 ms, max 12 ms, 2 consecutive steps).

host.clocks: jetson_clocks applied 2026-10-15 (all 14 CPUs 2601 MHz, CPU idle states off, EMC 4266 MHz, nvpmodel 120W); verified before each batch from /sys and recorded in the batch host.json
host.note: taskset pinning of the processes the runner starts; other host processes are not isolated (no isolcpus). Remote desktop disconnected during batches.

p4.purpose: P5 (supplementary pilot): RAPTOR's target interface in SITL. E1 flight direction vs the per-axis observation clipping at C->N; E2 single external-setpoint interruption (which branch, does T1 act on the in-flight timeout, target jump at resume); E3 repeated interruptions; E4 N->C during 2.0 m/s motion. Exploration, 1-2 runs per cell, no statistical conclusions.

independence.sim_seed: Every P4 batch run gets its own Gazebo seed (gz sim --seed): first 31 bits of sha256(batch prefix + run id + master_seed), recorded in plan.json, config.json and the Gazebo command line. Gazebo sensor noise (IMU, barometer, magnetometer) is drawn from this seed; without --seed it is drawn from std::random_device.

initial_yaw.rule: P5 draws no random heading. Conditions with initial_yaw_deg (E1 Y45: +45 deg) spawn the x500 at that fixed yaw; all others at yaw 0 (PX4 heading 96.0 deg) as P4 01b/01c.
initial_yaw.heading_rule: Gazebo yaw is counter-clockwise from East (ENU); PX4 heading is clockwise from North (NED) incl. the world magnetic declination. At spawn yaw 0 the PX4 heading is 96.0 deg (P3 batch-01 first C->N 95.99-96.05 deg; P4 dev-01 95.9 deg), so the expected heading before arming is 96.0 - initial_yaw_deg (tolerance 3 deg).

independence.hover_point: Not perturbed: the local frame origin is the spawn point and the Gazebo world is flat and translation invariant, so a horizontal offset of the hover point changes nothing the controllers or the physics see; the hover altitude stays the frozen 3 m (analysis references).
independence.verification: Before the batches: (1) startup-only runs with seeds A, A, B compare the at-rest raw gyro noise (sensor_gyro) sample by sample: same seed identical, different seed different; (2) development flights with different seeds/headings give different measured values; (3) every batch run checks that its Gazebo command carried the planned seed and that the heading at takeoff equals the planned heading (tolerance 3 deg).
independence.default_settings: The equivalence batch runs without --sim-seed/--initial-yaw-deg (as P3), i.e. the default settings.

statistics.group_ci: mean and two-sided 95% t interval (Student t, n-1 dof) over the runs of one group
statistics.ratio_ci: (N0 - Nx)/(N0 - baseline) from group means; 95% percentile bootstrap interval resampling runs with replacement within each of the three groups independently, 20000 resamples, numpy default_rng(master_seed); resamples with |N0 - baseline| < 1e-9 dropped
statistics.note: n = 5 (01a treatments) or 3 (01b, baselines); intervals describe run-to-run variation of this SITL setup under independent seeds and headings, not real-flight variation

p4.teacher_forcing_rule: N2 (RINI=4): the native inference steps immediately before the C->N owner change (inactive, teacher forced, consecutive) must number at least 10; checked per run from research_memory.

baseline_matching.rule: 01b RAPTOR baselines (M1, M2) must capture in the same state as the C->N of the same condition: |speed along +N at capture - C->N group mean| <= 0.05 m/s and |mean acceleration along +N over [capture - 50 ms, capture] - C->N group mean| <= 0.3 m/s^2. Checked in the batch audit; a baseline outside the window is reported and its ratios are marked unmatched (no re-run).
baseline_matching.m3_baseline: M3 has no own baseline: its second C->N happens in the same state as an M1 C->N (same profile, same axis), so the in-batch M1 RAPTOR baseline is its baseline (same batch, no splicing).

dev_latency.rule: 10 P4 runs (all kinds and conditions) on the final candidate before freezing; every run maximum applied-command age <= 8 ms with the frozen gate unchanged (P3 rule).

p4.equivalence: New candidate (MC_RAPTOR_RTGT=2 added; RTGT 0/1 code paths unchanged): P4 M1 N2 x2 (config/p4.json, RTGT=0 default) and P4-01c V1.0 T1 x2 (config/p4c.json, RTGT=1), each run with its own Gazebo seed; criteria in p5.equivalence.

host.note: taskset pinning of the processes the runner starts; other host processes are not isolated (no isolcpus). Remote desktop disconnected during batches.

p4c.purpose: E1 takeover-target evidence and metrics (tools/p4c_metrics.py, unchanged definitions).
p4c.memory_treatment: N2 (MC_RAPTOR_RINI=4) in every run: teacher forcing while inactive, GRU kept and previous action = classic last applied command at entry. Only the takeover target differs.

source_check.observation: mc_raptor.cpp observe(): position error = position - _trajectory_setpoint.position and velocity error = linear_velocity - _trajectory_setpoint.velocity (NED, FRD->FLU sign change), both rotated into the target-yaw frame (Rt_inv from _trajectory_setpoint.yaw), then clipped per axis to +-max_position_error (0.5 m) and +-max_velocity_error (1.0 m/s) (mc_raptor.hpp). The internal target's velocity therefore enters the observation; clipping is the last step before the observation is handed to the executor (research_memory.policy_input[0:3] position, [12:15] velocity).
source_check.capture: Run(): at activation reset() clears timestamp_last_trajectory_setpoint_set, so in the activation cycle the stale branch captures position, yaw (from the attitude) and zero velocity; afterwards the stale branch keeps that target until an external setpoint arrives. T1 hooks into exactly that capture (activation cycle only) and advances the target every following stale cycle.

parameters.gating: effective only with MC_RAPTOR_RSH=1 (all research code); RTGT=0 leaves the original code path unchanged (capture rows are logged only)

target_check.rule: Per run from research_target: exactly one activation capture at the C->N owner change (within 50 ms) with mode = planned RTGT and decel = planned RTDEC; T0: target velocity 0 and no profile rows; T1: initial target velocity = the vehicle_local_position sample RAPTOR used (vx, vy; vertical 0), every profile row equal to the closed-form profile (speed0 - a t along the captured direction, position the integral), phase change at speed0/a, final point at speed0^2/(2a); the state read after entry equals the logged target of that cycle.

clipping.definition: research_memory inference rows while RAPTOR is active in [change, window end]: a component is clipped when |value| >= limit*(1-1e-6). Reported separately for position and velocity: rows, total duration (zero-order hold to the next row), first and last clipped time after the change, longest continuous span.

settle.definition: first vehicle_local_position sample (timestamp_sample) after the change from which the 3D speed stays below 0.1 m/s until the window end (change + post_handover_s); settle time from the change; distance = horizontal and along-axis distance from the position at the change to the position at the settle time. None if the speed is not below the threshold at the window end or the flight failed.

capture_cost_reference.definition: At 1.0 m/s the capture part of the C->N cost is the absolute value of the acceleration-matched 01b M1 RAPTOR baseline (zero-velocity capture with intact memory; 01b: 86% of the N0 step, 93% of the altitude loss, 99% of the tilt). Part of it removed by T1 = (T0 - T1) / baseline, T0 and T1 from batch 01c (both N2 memory), 95% bootstrap over the three groups. In-batch T0 is compared with 01b M1 N2 (same profile and memory). Cross-batch reference as requested, not an acceptance splice.

offline_reference.source: out-of-repo l2f simulation with mc_raptor error clipping (position +-0.5 m, velocity +-1 m/s), user correction 2026-10-16
offline_reference.zero_velocity_capture: no flip at >=3 m/s, but tilt above 45 deg from 2 m/s on (matches P2 SITL explore-02); about 0.9 m altitude loss at 5 m/s for the heavy airframe

p4c.statistics: per group (level x target) mean and 95% t interval over the runs that did not fail (n reported); T0 - T1 difference with 95% percentile bootstrap (20000 resamples, numpy default_rng(master_seed)); flight failures counted per group.

equivalence.purpose: New candidate (adds MC_RAPTOR_RTGT/RTDEC and research_target) with RTGT=0 must reproduce P2 S1 and P4 01b M1 before P4-01c.
equivalence.metric_rule: each run inside [min - t, max + t] of the reference group with the same kind, condition and treatment, t = max(tolerance, half the reference spread)
required: P2 entry and teacher-forcing evidence VERIFIED, capture activation_reset_hold with zero target velocity
written GRU norm (N2) inside the reference range (tolerance 0.05)
MC_RAPTOR_RTGT = 0 in force, research_target activation capture with mode 0 and zero target velocity, no profile rows

dev_latency.rule: 10 P4-01c runs (every level and target) on the final candidate before freezing; every run maximum applied-command age <= 8 ms with the frozen gate unchanged (P3/P4 rule). A pre-registered flight failure (2.0 m/s T0) is a result; the following runs confirm a clean restart after the runner safety abort.

p5.purpose: P5 E2/E3 (kind p5_gap): RAPTOR tracks a runner-published straight line at 2.0 m/s through its external trajectory_setpoint input; the runner stops publishing for D s and then resumes on the same time-parameterized line (the target jumps back to the current trajectory point), once (E2) or six times with 0.3 s of restored link between (E3). After the cruise the line decelerates to rest; the stream ends at rest, RAPTOR holds, then the classic AUTO_LOITER takes over and lands. N2 memory at the setup entry. T0: original in-flight timeout capture (zero velocity, RTGT=0); T1: speed-matched target also at in-flight timeout captures (RTGT=2) with deceleration 2.0 (T1), 1.0 (T1a1) or 3.0 (T1a3) m/s^2.

motor_saturation.note: actuator_motors control in [0,1]; upper/lower limit within 1e-3

profile.note: Profile time: reposition from RAPTOR's hover capture to the start offset (-L/2 along the axis, trapezoid 1.0 m/s, 0.5 m/s^2), hold 3 s, 1 s linear ramp to 2.0 m/s, cruise = pre_gap_s + count*D + (count-1)*recover + post_gap_s, linear deceleration to rest at decel_m_s2, then end_hold_s of stationary setpoints. Gap k covers profile times [cruise start + pre_gap_s + k*(D + recover), + D); no setpoint is published inside a gap; the trajectory time keeps running.

D0.3-A0.description: E2: single interruption D = 0.3 s at 2.0 m/s after 1.0 s of cruise, then 3.0 s of restored link before the deceleration; +N

D0.3-A45.description: E2: single interruption D = 0.3 s at 2.0 m/s after 1.0 s of cruise, then 3.0 s of restored link before the deceleration; north-east

D0.7-A0.description: E2: single interruption D = 0.7 s at 2.0 m/s after 1.0 s of cruise, then 3.0 s of restored link before the deceleration; +N

D0.7-A45.description: E2: single interruption D = 0.7 s at 2.0 m/s after 1.0 s of cruise, then 3.0 s of restored link before the deceleration; north-east

D1.0-A0.description: E2: single interruption D = 1.0 s at 2.0 m/s after 1.0 s of cruise, then 3.0 s of restored link before the deceleration; +N

D1.0-A45.description: E2: single interruption D = 1.0 s at 2.0 m/s after 1.0 s of cruise, then 3.0 s of restored link before the deceleration; north-east

D1.5-A0.description: E2: single interruption D = 1.5 s at 2.0 m/s after 1.0 s of cruise, then 3.0 s of restored link before the deceleration; +N

D1.5-A45.description: E2: single interruption D = 1.5 s at 2.0 m/s after 1.0 s of cruise, then 3.0 s of restored link before the deceleration; north-east

R6-A0.description: E3: six interruptions of 0.5 s with 0.3 s of restored link after each (cycle 0.8 s), 2.0 m/s, 1.0 s of cruise before the first; the deceleration starts at the end of the sixth cycle; +N

R6-A45.description: E3: six interruptions of 0.5 s with 0.3 s of restored link after each (cycle 0.8 s), 2.0 m/s, 1.0 s of cruise before the first; the deceleration starts at the end of the sixth cycle; north-east

T0.description: N2 memory; original RAPTOR in-flight setpoint-timeout capture: current position and yaw, zero velocity (MC_RAPTOR_RTGT=0)

T1.description: N2 memory; speed-matched target at activation and at every in-flight setpoint-timeout capture (MC_RAPTOR_RTGT=2), 2.0 m/s^2

planned_path_check.rule: Before the motion: max(|start point|, |end point|) of the planned line (ramp + cruise + deceleration to rest, centred on RAPTOR's hover capture) + 1.0 m margin + interruption drift <= safety_radius_m - radius_margin_m = 8 m. Interruption drift = max(0, v*0.2 s (frozen setpoint before the timeout) + v^2/(2*1.0 m/s^2) (slowest T1 target) - trajectory distance from the last gap start to the end point); it is 0 for every condition because the vehicle cannot pass the still-moving trajectory point during a gap. A condition that does not fit is not flown.

gap_timing.rule: per gap, the setpoint-free interval (setpoint arrivals = logged trajectory_setpoint rows merged with raptor_status reception cycles: first arrival after the gap minus last arrival before it) must lie in [D - 0.01 s, D + 0.06 s] (one 20 ms setpoint period plus runner pump granularity); RAPTOR must make exactly one in-flight capture per gap (research_target KIND_CAPTURE, activation 0) 200-216 ms after the last arrival (200 ms timeout counted from RAPTOR's reception cycle, which follows the arrival within one 4 ms cycle, plus the 4 ms cycle quantization of the timeout), with the planned mode and deceleration; T1: profile rows equal to the closed-form profile and an END row (external setpoint) at the resume; T0: zero target velocity and no profile rows.

catch_up.rule: after a resume: first time from which RAPTOR's observed horizontal position error and velocity error (research_memory.policy_input [0:2] and [12:14], the exact executor input, relative to the latest received setpoint) stay <= 0.2 m and <= 0.2 m/s for 0.5 s; searched until the next gap or the end of the cruise (E2: 3.0 s); none if not reached. Both thresholds are below the clipping limits, so the clipped input equals the true error when the criterion holds.

settle.definition: first vehicle_local_position sample (timestamp_sample) after the change from which the 3D speed stays below 0.1 m/s until the window end (change + post_handover_s); settle time from the change; distance = horizontal and along-axis distance from the position at the change to the position at the settle time. None if the speed is not below the threshold at the window end or the flight failed.

clipping.definition: research_memory inference rows while RAPTOR is active in [change, window end]: a component is clipped when |value| >= limit*(1-1e-6). Reported separately for position and velocity: rows, total duration (zero-order hold to the next row), first and last clipped time after the change, longest continuous span.

failure_criteria.safety_envelope: any of tilt >= 45 deg, angular-rate component >= 8 rad/s, horizontal radius >= 10 m, altitude >= 8 m (frozen safety envelope; reaching the limit counts), or a runner safety abort
failure_criteria.no_joint_recovery: joint recovery not SETTLED within 10 s after the actual change (frozen P0 thresholds, active controller target)
failure_criteria.motor_saturation: any motor at >=0.999 or <=0.001 continuously for at least 0.5 s inside [trigger, window end]
failure_criteria.window: [first gap start, end of the post_stream phase] (truncated at an abort); no_joint_recovery is judged from RAPTOR's capture after the final stream stop at rest (frozen P0 thresholds) instead of an owner change
